description.en: The backhand raise is a lateral raise variation performed with the wrists rotated so the back of the hand leads the lift. The reverse grip changes the angle of pull on the deltoid, hitting the medial and rear delts from a different angle than standard lateral raises. It is a useful variation for breaking through shoulder plateaus.

en: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Rotate your wrists so the backs of your hands face forward.
Maintain a slight bend in the elbows throughout.
Brace your core and stand tall.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides with the back of the hand leading the lift.
Continue until the dumbbells reach shoulder height.
Squeeze the medial and rear delts at the top.
Lower the dumbbells back down with control.
Different angle than standard lateral raise
Hits medial and rear delts
Useful for breaking through shoulder plateaus
Builds shoulder width and definition
Strong rotator cuff engagement
Easy to scale by changing dumbbell weight

description.en: The balance board is a stability training tool where you stand on an unstable tilting platform (rocker board, wobble board, or Bosu ball) and maintain balance. It develops proprioception, ankle stability, and neuromuscular control. It is widely used in rehabilitation and athletic training.

en: Place a balance board, rocker board, or Bosu ball (flat side up) on a non-slip surface.
Carefully step onto the board with both feet. Position feet hip-width apart.
Find your balance. Engage your core and ankle stabilizers.
Try to keep the board level — do not let the edges touch the floor.
Hold the balanced position for 30 to 60 seconds.
For progression: close your eyes, stand on one leg, add small squats, or catch and throw a ball.
Use a wall or chair nearby for safety when first learning.
Practice 3 to 5 sets per session.
Develops proprioception and body awareness
Builds ankle stability and control
Useful for rehabilitation after ankle injuries
Improves neuromuscular control
Engages deep stabilizer muscles
Widely used in physical therapy and sport training

description.en: The band vertical Pallof press uses a resistance band anchored either high or low for anti-rotation core training in a vertical plane. Pressing the band straight up or down while resisting the rotational pull trains the core through a different plane than the standard horizontal Pallof press.

en: Anchor a resistance band to a high or low point on your side.
Stand perpendicular to the anchor with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grip the band end with both hands at chest level.
Step away from the anchor to create band tension.
Brace your core hard against the rotational pull.
Press the band straight up or straight down depending on anchor position.
Hold the press for one count while resisting the band pull.
Bring your hands back to your chest with control. Complete reps, switch sides.
Vertical plane anti-rotation training
Different stimulus than horizontal Pallof press
Builds core stability
Strong oblique engagement
Useful for athletes who need core stability
Easy to scale by changing band tension

description.en: The barbell incline shoulder raise is performed lying face down on an incline bench with a barbell hanging straight down. You raise the bar forward and up in a front raise pattern. The chest support eliminates body english and the angle creates unique loading on the front delts and upper chest.

en: Set an incline bench to 30 to 45 degrees. Lie face down on the bench with chest supported.
Hold a light barbell hanging below the bench, arms extended toward the floor.
Raise the bar forward and upward by lifting your arms in a front raise motion.
Continue until the bar is at face height.
Squeeze your front delts at the top.
Lower under control back to hanging position.
The chest support eliminates momentum.
Use light weight. Aim for 10 to 15 reps.
Strict front delt isolation from chest-supported position
Eliminates body english
Unique angle for shoulder loading
Builds front delts and upper chest
Easy to load progressively
Different stimulus from standing front raises

description.en: The barbell single leg good morning is a unilateral version of the classic good morning. With a barbell across the upper back, you hinge at the hips while balancing on one leg with the other extended back. The single-leg pattern challenges balance and corrects strength imbalances in the posterior chain.

en: Position a light barbell across your upper back behind the neck.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back.
Shift your weight to your right leg.
Hinge at the hips and lower your torso forward.
As you hinge, lift the left leg back behind you for balance.
Continue until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glute to return to standing. Switch sides after the set.
Unilateral posterior chain work
Develops balance
Corrects strength imbalances
Builds hamstrings and glutes
Strong erector spinae engagement
Useful for athletic conditioning

description.en: The basic toe touch is the most fundamental hamstring stretch. The lifter stands tall and folds forward at the hips reaching the hands down toward the toes. It stretches the hamstrings, calves, and lower back in one simple move.

en: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Brace your core lightly.
Keep a slight bend in the knees if needed.
Hinge at the hips to fold the torso forward over the legs.
Reach your hands down toward your toes.
Allow the head to hang relaxed.
Feel the stretch through the hamstrings and back.
Hold for several breaths then come back up slowly.
Stretches the hamstrings
Releases lower back tension
No equipment needed
Easy to add to any routine
Useful warm-up move
Strong fundamental stretch

description.en: The battling ropes half kneeling is a battle rope wave drill done from a half kneeling position. The kneeling stance challenges core stability and removes leg drive. It builds shoulder endurance and core strength under load.

en: Grip both battle rope ends with the arms at the sides.
Kneel in a half kneeling position with one knee down.
Square the hips to the anchor.
Brace your core and keep the chest up.
Begin alternating wave slams with the rope ends.
Keep the half kneeling position stable throughout.
Maintain a fast tempo on the waves.
Continue for the working set.
Burns calories
Builds core stability
Strong conditioning move
Trains the shoulders
Useful for athletes

description.en: The bodyweight pulse squat performs short pulse reps at the bottom of the squat range. By moving up only a few inches before pulsing back down, you keep continuous tension on the quads and glutes. The pulses build muscular endurance and create a strong burn in the legs.

en: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold your arms out in front for balance.
Squat down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
From the parallel position, rise up only a few inches.
Drop back down to the parallel squat position.
Continue pulsing in the bottom range with short reps.
Maintain an upright torso and bracing throughout.
Continue for the duration of the set.
Continuous tension on quads and glutes
Builds muscular endurance
Strong leg burn
No equipment required
Useful as a finisher
Easy to scale by changing depth

description.en: The cable lateral lunge is a frontal-plane lunge variation performed at a low cable pulley. You hold a handle and step laterally to one side, sinking into a lateral lunge against the cable tension. The cable provides constant resistance throughout the lunge, building hip and inner-thigh strength.

en: Set a cable pulley to a low position. Attach a D-handle.
Stand sideways to the cable. Grip the handle with the hand closest to the cable, then bring it to your chest.
Step away from the cable until you feel tension. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Take a wide step to the side away from the cable with your far leg.
Sit your far hip back and bend your far knee, lowering into a lateral squat on that side.
Keep your near (close to cable) leg straight, foot flat on the floor.
Drive through your far foot to push back to standing.
Repeat for the desired reps, then switch sides. Use moderate weight.
Builds frontal-plane hip strength
Constant cable tension throughout
Targets the adductors and glutes
Trains lateral stability
Carries over to athletic cutting movements
Easy to load progressively

description.en: The cable preacher curl combines the strict arm-braced position of the preacher bench with constant cable tension throughout the range of motion. The cable maintains load at both the top and bottom of the curl, creating one of the most effective bicep isolation setups available.

en: Position a preacher bench in front of a low cable pulley. Attach a straight bar or EZ bar.
Sit on the bench with upper arms draped over the pad. Grip the cable attachment with an underhand grip.
Start with arms nearly extended. The cable should be under tension.
Curl the bar up by bending at the elbows. Keep upper arms pressed into the pad.
Continue until forearms are roughly vertical. Squeeze your biceps hard.
Lower under control. Maintain cable tension throughout — do not let slack develop.
Stop just before full elbow extension to maintain tension.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Constant cable tension throughout the full range
Preacher bench eliminates all body english
Loads the bottom stretch better than dumbbell preacher curls
Excellent for high-rep bicep isolation
Easy to load progressively
Builds bicep strength at the lengthened position

description.en: The cable pull-through is a hip-hinge exercise performed at a low cable pulley with a rope attachment. You stand facing away from the cable, pass the rope between your legs, and hinge forward and back to load the glutes and hamstrings. The cable provides constant tension and peaks at the lockout, making it one of the best glute exercises.

en: Attach a rope to a low cable pulley. Stand facing away from the machine, straddling the cable.
Reach between your legs and grip the rope with both hands.
Step forward until the rope is taut. Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width apart.
Hinge forward at the hips, letting the rope pull your hands back between your legs. Keep your back flat.
Feel a stretch in your hamstrings. Brace your core. Knees stay slightly bent throughout.
Snap your hips forward by squeezing your glutes hard. Stand fully tall at lockout.
The cable tension peaks at lockout, loading the glutes maximally at full hip extension.
Lower under control. Repeat for 12 to 20 reps per set.
Constant cable tension peaks at glute lockout
Excellent glute and hamstring developer
Teaches the hip-hinge pattern effectively
Easier on the lower back than barbell hip hinges
Easy to load progressively
Useful for learning the hip hinge before deadlifts

description.en: The cable rear drive is a rear deltoid exercise where you stand facing a cable at mid-height and pull the handle straight back behind you with a straight arm, driving the arm back past your hip. It targets the rear delt through a shoulder extension arc rather than a fly arc.

en: Set a cable to chest or shoulder height. Attach a D-handle.
Face the cable. Grip the handle with one hand, arm extended forward.
Step back for tension.
Pull the handle straight back past your hip by driving your arm behind you. Keep your arm straight.
Squeeze your rear delt and lat at the end position.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Complete reps, then switch arms.
Aim for 12 to 15 reps per side.
Targets the rear delt through extension arc
Different stimulus than fly or row patterns
Constant cable tension
Easy to load progressively
Builds rear delt and lat together
Strict unilateral isolation

description.en: The dumbbell tricep kickback is an isolation exercise performed bent at the waist with a dumbbell in one or both hands. You extend the dumbbell back behind you by straightening at the elbow, with the upper arm held fixed parallel to the floor. The strict position with the elbow above the body makes it one of the few tricep exercises where the long head is fully shortened at peak contraction.

en: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Hinge forward at the hips with a slight knee bend until your torso is roughly 45 degrees from horizontal.
Pin both upper arms against your sides so they are parallel to the floor. Your elbows should be bent 90 degrees with the dumbbells hanging down.
Brace your core and lock in your back angle. Keep your back flat throughout.
Extend both arms back by straightening at the elbows. Keep your upper arms completely still — only the forearms move.
End with arms fully extended behind you, dumbbells slightly above hip level. Squeeze your triceps hard for one second.
Bend the elbows under control to return to the starting 90-degree position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps. Use light weight — strict form matters far more than load on this lift.
Forces strict isolation of the triceps with no body english possible
Peak contraction position fully shortens the tricep
Excellent finisher for tricep workouts
Builds the lateral and long heads of the triceps
Easy on the elbows and shoulders
Works at home with one pair of dumbbells

description.en: The dumbbell lying rear lateral raise is a rear deltoid exercise performed lying face down on an incline or flat bench, raising dumbbells out to the sides. The prone position eliminates momentum for strict rear delt isolation.

en: Lie face down on an incline bench (30 to 45 degrees) with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down below the bench.
Raise both dumbbells out to the sides with elbows slightly bent.
Lift until your arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your rear delts at the top.
Lower under control.
Your chest on the bench eliminates all momentum.
Use light weight. Aim for 12 to 15 reps.
Strict rear delt isolation from prone position
Eliminates all momentum and body english
Builds shoulder balance
Light weight is very effective
Easy to set up
Useful for shoulder health

description.en: The dumbbell lying supine curl is performed lying face up on a bench with the arms hanging over the side. The position fully stretches the biceps at the bottom of each rep and eliminates body english entirely. It is one of the strictest possible bicep variations.

en: Lie face up on a flat bench with your arms hanging off the side.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing forward (underhand grip).
Allow your arms to fully extend below the bench.
Pin your back to the bench and brace your core.
Curl the dumbbells up by bending at the elbows.
Keep your upper arms in line with your torso.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top.
Lower the dumbbells back down with control to a full stretch below the bench.
Maximum stretch on the biceps
Eliminates all body english
Strict isolation of the biceps
Different angle than seated incline curls
Strong long-head bicep emphasis
Useful for breaking through bicep plateaus

description.en: The dumbbell one-arm seated neutral wrist curl targets the brachioradialis and radial forearm by curling a dumbbell with a neutral (thumbs-up) grip from a seated position. The neutral grip shifts emphasis from the standard flexors to the radial side of the forearm.

en: Sit on a bench. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand.
Rest your right forearm on your right thigh with your thumb pointing up (neutral grip).
Let the dumbbell hang off your knee with wrist extended outward.
Curl the dumbbell up by flexing your wrist toward your thumb (radial deviation).
Squeeze the top of your forearm.
Lower under control.
Complete reps, then switch sides.
Use light weight. Aim for 15 to 20 reps.
Targets the brachioradialis and radial forearm
Builds forearm thickness from the side profile
Neutral grip is wrist-friendly
Easy to scale progressively
Simple setup
Useful for complete forearm development

description.en: The dumbbell pullover is a unique single-joint exercise performed lying across a bench with a single dumbbell held over the chest. The arms travel in a wide arc overhead and back, providing a deep stretch and contraction across both the lats and the chest. It is a classic bodybuilding exercise that hits multiple muscles in a way no other lift quite matches.

en: Place a single dumbbell at the end of a flat bench.
Lie perpendicular across the bench so only your upper back is supported, with your hips dropped lower than your shoulders.
Plant both feet firmly on the floor for stability.
Pick up the dumbbell with both hands cupped under the upper plate (like holding a goblet). Press it straight up over your chest with arms slightly bent.
Maintain a fixed, slight bend in your elbows throughout the entire movement. Do not bend or straighten the elbows during the rep.
Lower the dumbbell in an arc back over your head, going as far as your shoulder mobility allows. Feel the stretch across your lats and chest at the bottom.
Reverse the arc by pulling the dumbbell back over your chest, contracting your lats and chest hard.
Repeat for the desired number of reps. Use a moderate weight — form and stretch matter more than load on this lift.
Provides a unique deep stretch across the lats and chest
One of the only exercises that trains the lats and chest in the same movement
Improves shoulder and rib-cage mobility
Builds size in the lats, chest, and serratus anterior
Works at home with a single dumbbell and bench
Joint-friendly when performed with light to moderate weight

description.en: The dumbbell standing single arm Arnold press is a single-arm Arnold press performed standing. The rotating press hits all three deltoid heads in one rep while the standing position adds core engagement. The single-arm load creates a strong anti-rotation challenge for the obliques.

en: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a single dumbbell in your right hand at chin level.
Start with palm facing your body, dumbbell close to your shoulder.
Brace your core hard and pull your shoulder back.
Press the dumbbell overhead while rotating the wrist outward.
End with palm facing forward at the top.
Lock out at the top with arm fully extended.
Reverse the rotation as you lower back to the starting position. Switch arms.
Hits all three deltoid heads
Strong anti-rotation core challenge
Standing position adds core engagement
Corrects shoulder imbalances
Builds total shoulder size
Useful for athletic carryover

description.en: The dumbbell wood chop squat combines a squat with a wood chop performed during the descent. As you squat down, you chop the dumbbell from a high overhead position diagonally down across your body. The combo trains rotational core strength, hip mobility, and leg drive in one rep.

en: Hold a single dumbbell with both hands above one shoulder, arms extended.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and pivot slightly toward the dumbbell.
As you squat down, chop the dumbbell diagonally across your body to the opposite hip.
Rotate your torso through the chop, keeping arms long.
At the bottom, you should be in a squat with the dumbbell down by your opposite hip.
Drive up through your heels while reversing the chop back to the starting overhead position.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
Trains rotational core strength under load
Builds leg drive linked to core rotation
Hits obliques heavily
Strong functional carryover to throwing and rotational sports
Time-efficient combo movement
Improves hip and trunk coordination

description.en: The dynamic chest stretch is a warm-up exercise where you swing both arms backward (and forward) in a controlled motion to dynamically open the chest and front shoulders. Unlike static stretches, the dynamic motion warms up the muscles, increases blood flow, and prepares the body for movement.

en: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Extend both arms forward at shoulder height.
Brace your core gently.
Swing both arms back as far as comfortable, opening your chest.
Pause briefly at the back of the swing.
Bring your arms back forward, crossing them at the chest if comfortable.
Continue swinging back and forward in a controlled rhythm.
Move at a moderate pace — not ballistic.
Perform 10 to 15 reps as part of a warm-up.
Dynamically warms up the chest and front shoulders
Increases blood flow before training
Improves shoulder mobility
Excellent pre-workout warm-up
No equipment needed
Engaging and active

description.en: Elbow to knee is a standing core exercise where you bring opposite elbow and knee together by rotating and crunching. It is the same as the standing air bike or standing bicycle crunch — targeting obliques from a standing position.

en: Stand with hands behind your head.
Lift right knee while rotating left elbow toward it.
Crunch to make contact or come close.
Return to standing. Switch sides.
Continue alternating at a brisk pace.
Rotate your torso with each crunch.
Aim for 15 to 20 total reps.
Useful warm-up or circuit exercise.
Standing oblique exercise — no floor needed
Cardiovascular conditioning
No equipment needed
Quick and accessible
Builds coordination
Useful for circuits

description.en: The elevated seated calf raise is performed seated with the balls of the feet on an elevated surface. The heels drop below the platform for a deep calf stretch then press up to the top. The seated position with bent knees biases the soleus over the gastrocnemius.

en: Sit on a bench or chair with feet flat on the floor.
Place a sturdy block or plate in front of you.
Rest the balls of both feet on top of the block.
Let your heels hang below the level of the block.
Brace your core and keep your back upright.
Press through the balls of the feet to lift the heels as high as possible.
Squeeze the calves hard at the top.
Lower with control back to a deep heel stretch.
Targets the soleus
Full range of motion
Deep calf stretch
No machine required
Easy to load with weight on lap
Useful for calf detail

description.en: The forward bend back stretch is a basic standing forward fold for the back and hamstrings. The lifter stands tall and folds forward at the hips letting the upper body hang. It is a strong cool down stretch for tight backs and hamstrings.

en: Stand tall with feet hip width apart.
Brace your core and lengthen the spine up.
Hinge forward at the hips with a long spine.
Continue folding forward toward the floor.
Let the head and arms hang heavy.
Hold the lower legs or floor with the hands.
Hold the stretch with steady breath letting gravity deepen it.
Roll up slowly to standing one vertebra at a time.
Stretches the hamstrings
Releases the lower back
No equipment needed
Useful cool down move
Easy to do anywhere
Trains hip mobility

description.en: The front leg lift under knee tap is a low impact cardio drill that combines a high knee march with a hand tap under the thigh. The exaggerated movement raises the heart rate while training hip flexor and core control.

en: Stand tall with the feet hip width apart.
Hold the arms relaxed at the sides.
Brace the core and keep the chest up.
Lift one knee high to the front.
Reach the opposite hand under the thigh and tap.
Lower the leg back to the floor.
Repeat on the other side with the opposite hand and knee.
Continue alternating for the working set.
Elevates the heart rate.
Trains hip flexor mobility.
Loads the core for stability.
Low impact cardio option.
Useful warm-up drill.

description.en: The glute ham developer hip extension is a posterior chain builder done on a glute ham developer. The lifter lies face down with the legs hanging and lifts them up. It loads the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back together.

en: Lie face down on a glute ham developer.
Set the hips on the pad and the chest forward.
Let the legs hang down off the back.
Hold the front handles for stability.
Brace your core and keep the chest up.
Lift the legs up to parallel with the floor.
Squeeze the glutes and hamstrings at the top.
Lower with control to the start.
Builds the posterior chain
Strong GHD variation
Trains the glutes
Useful for athletes
Builds the hamstrings

description.en: The inverted row on a bench elevates the feet on a bench during inverted rows. The elevated feet shift more bodyweight onto the arms, increasing difficulty. It is a progression from standard flat-foot inverted rows toward weighted rows or pull-ups.

en: Set a bar at about hip height. Place a bench nearby for your feet.
Lie underneath the bar. Grip with an overhand grip. Place your heels on the bench.
Body forms a straight line from heels to head.
Pull your chest toward the bar.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower under control.
The elevated feet make this harder than flat-foot rows.
Aim for 8 to 12 reps.
Increased difficulty from elevated feet
Greater pulling demand per rep
Progressive from flat-foot inverted rows
Builds toward weighted rows and pull-ups
Simple setup
Develops back pulling strength

description.en: The jump squat is a plyometric exercise where you perform a bodyweight squat and explode upward into a jump at the top. It builds explosive lower-body power, fast-twitch muscle fibers, and cardiovascular conditioning. It is a staple exercise in HIIT, athletic training, and CrossFit.

en: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out. Arms at your sides or in front.
Sit your hips down and back into a squat — at least to parallel or deeper.
From the bottom of the squat, explode upward by extending your hips, knees, and ankles.
Swing your arms up to generate extra momentum. Leave the ground at the top.
Jump as high as you can. Fully extend your body at the peak.
Land softly with bent knees to absorb the impact. Let your hips sit back into the squat landing position.
Immediately drop into the next squat and jump again.
Perform for time (20 to 45 seconds) or reps (8 to
per set.
Builds explosive lower-body power
Develops fast-twitch muscle fibers
Excellent cardiovascular conditioning
No equipment needed — works anywhere
Carries over to sprinting and jumping performance
Time-efficient HIIT exercise

description.en: The kettlebell one-arm clean and jerk (also called long cycle) combines a single-arm clean with a jerk in one continuous movement. You swing the KB from between your legs to the front rack (clean), then immediately drive it overhead (jerk). It is the ultimate kettlebell endurance exercise.

en: Stand with a KB between your feet. Hinge and grip it with one hand.
Swing the KB back between your legs, then drive your hips forward to clean it to the front rack.
Immediately dip your knees and drive the KB overhead with explosive leg drive (jerk).
Lock out overhead. Stand tall.
Lower the KB back to the rack, then let it swing back between your legs.
Continue for the desired reps without setting the KB down.
Switch hands at the halfway point.
This is the most demanding KB exercise — pace yourself.
Ultimate KB endurance exercise
Combines clean and jerk in one flow
Builds total-body explosive power and conditioning
Competition lift in kettlebell sport
Develops pacing and mental toughness
Burns calories at a very high rate

description.en: The kettlebell standing calf raise is performed standing with a kettlebell in each hand. By raising up onto the balls of the feet against the kettlebell load, you train the calves directly with progressive resistance. It is a strong choice for home training without a calf machine.

en: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
Place the balls of your feet on a small platform or weight plate for elevation.
Allow your heels to hang off the platform.
Brace your core and stand tall.
Lower your heels below the platform level for a stretch.
Raise your heels as high as possible by pushing through the balls of your feet.
Squeeze your calves hard at the top.
Lower back down with control.
Heavy loaded calf training
Strong stretch with elevated foot position
No machine required
Builds calf size and strength
Allows progressive loading
Useful for home training

description.en: The kneeling chest stretch is a deep chest-opening stretch performed from a kneeling position. With arms extended behind you or placed on an elevated surface, you lean forward to stretch the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid. The kneeling position provides a stable base for a deeper stretch than standing variations.

en: Kneel on the floor facing a bench, chair, or elevated surface.
Place both hands on the surface behind you (or clasp them behind your back).
Keep your knees under your hips. Sit upright initially.
Lean forward while keeping your arms extended behind you. Your chest should open up.
Feel the deep stretch across your chest and front shoulders.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply into the stretch.
Return to the starting position slowly.
Repeat two to three times.
Deeply stretches the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid
Kneeling position provides a stable base
Counteracts forward-hunched posture
Improves shoulder flexibility for pressing exercises
No equipment needed (elevated surface optional)
Gentle enough for daily practice

description.en: The kneeling pulse performs small pulse movements at the top of a kneeling glute lift position. From a quadruped start, you lift one leg behind you with the knee bent, then perform short pulse lifts at the top. The continuous pulses create maximum glute time under tension and burnout.

en: Get into a quadruped position on hands and knees.
Position your hands shoulder-width apart and knees under hips.
Lift your right knee up and back behind you, knee bent at 90 degrees.
Press the heel up toward the ceiling.
Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Lower the leg slightly without touching the floor.
Pulse the leg up and down in short controlled motions.
Maintain constant glute tension. Switch sides after the set.
Maximum glute time under tension
Burnout finishing exercise
Builds glute size
No equipment required
Strong mind-muscle connection
Useful for glute specialization

description.en: The kneeling shoulder tap push up combines a kneeling push up with a shoulder tap. The lifter performs a push up from the knees and taps the opposite shoulder with one hand at the top. The shoulder tap adds anti-rotation core demand.

en: Begin in a high plank position from the knees.
Set the hands under the shoulders and the body in a straight line.
Brace your core hard.
Lower the chest toward the floor by bending the elbows.
Press back up to lockout.
At the top lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder.
Place the hand back down.
Repeat with the other hand on the next rep.
Beginner friendly chest move
Trains anti-rotation core
Builds shoulder stability
No equipment needed
Useful chest builder
Easy to scale

description.en: The lever seated full crunch is performed on a seated ab crunch machine that lets you crunch against a fixed load. The seated position eliminates lower back stress and lets you focus purely on the abs. The constant resistance through a full range builds ab thickness.

en: Sit on the ab crunch machine with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles or place your arms over the chest pad.
Adjust the seat height so the pad sits across your chest.
Brace your core and keep your hips planted.
Crunch your torso forward by contracting the abs.
Continue forward until you feel a strong contraction.
Squeeze the abs hard at the bottom.
Return slowly to the start, controlling the eccentric.
Loads the abs with constant resistance
Stable, guided path
Reduces lower back stress
Builds ab thickness
Easy to load progressively
Useful for ab hypertrophy

description.en: The lever seated left side crunch is an oblique builder performed on a seated ab crunch machine angled for one side. The lifter sits and crunches the torso to the left, loading the left obliques against the lever resistance. The machine isolates the obliques.

en: Sit on a lever ab crunch machine with the resistance set.
Position the body so the left side faces the lever.
Grip the handles and set the chest pad against the torso.
Brace your core and set the feet under the foot pads.
Crunch the torso to the left bending sideways.
Squeeze the left obliques hard at the bottom.
Hold briefly at the contracted position.
Return to the start with control. Complete reps.
Strong oblique isolation
Constant lever resistance
Easy to scale loading
Builds the obliques
Useful core builder
Strong machine move

description.en: The mid air lateral raises with switching palms is a bodyweight delt drill. Holding the arms out to the sides at shoulder height and rotating the palms up and down loads the side delts isometrically with a rotational element.

en: Stand tall with the feet shoulder width apart.
Raise both arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Keep the arms straight with a slight elbow bend.
Brace the core and keep the shoulders down.
Rotate both palms to face down.
Then rotate both palms to face up.
Continue switching the palm position while holding the arms up.
Continue for the working set.
Trains the side delts isometrically.
Adds rotation to the shoulder hold.
No equipment required.
Useful shoulder warm-up.
Builds shoulder endurance.

description.en: The peroneals stretch targets the peroneal muscles on the outer side of the lower leg — the muscles that evert the ankle (turn the sole of the foot outward). They get tight from running, lateral movement, and ankle instability. The stretch involves rolling the foot inward (inversion) to lengthen these muscles.

en: Sit on the floor with your right leg extended. Cross your left ankle over your right thigh.
Use your right hand to grip the top of your left foot.
Gently roll your left foot inward — bring the sole of your foot to face the ceiling.
You should feel a stretch along the outer side of your left lower leg and ankle.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply.
Release and shake out your foot. Switch sides.
For a standing version: cross one foot over the other and roll the top foot inward.
Repeat two to three times per side.
Stretches the peroneal muscles on the outer calf
Improves ankle inversion mobility
Relieves tightness from lateral movement and running
Helps prevent ankle injuries
Useful for athletes in court sports
No equipment needed

description.en: The PVC pass-through (shoulder dislocate with a stick) holds a PVC pipe or broomstick with a wide grip and rotates it from in front of the body, over the head, and behind the back in a smooth arc. It is the gold-standard shoulder mobility exercise.

en: Hold a PVC pipe, broomstick, or band with a very wide overhand grip in front of your thighs.
Keep your arms straight throughout.
Raise the stick up overhead and continue the arc behind your back.
The stick should travel from front → overhead → behind in one smooth motion.
Reverse the motion back to the front.
Start with a very wide grip. Narrow over time as mobility improves.
If any point feels painful, widen your grip.
Perform 10 to 15 pass-throughs as a warm-up.
Gold-standard shoulder mobility exercise
Improves shoulder flexion and extension range
Warms up the entire shoulder complex
Easy to track progress by grip width
Minimal equipment needed
Used by Olympic lifters worldwide

description.en: The resistance band front plank with single arm pulldown anchors a band overhead. From a plank position, one hand pulls the band down toward the hip while the body resists rotation.

en: Anchor a resistance band to a sturdy point overhead.
Set up in a high plank facing away from the anchor.
Grab the band with one hand keeping the arm extended overhead.
Brace the core and keep the body in a straight line.
Pull the band down toward the same side hip by driving the elbow back.
Resist rotation through the torso as you pull.
Return the arm overhead with control.
Repeat for all reps then switch sides.
Trains the lats and core together.
Builds anti rotation strength.
Plank position improves shoulder stability.
Carryover to athletic performance.
Develops total body coordination.
Easy to scale by adjusting band tension.

description.en: The lever seated horizontal leg press is performed on a horizontal leg press machine where you sit upright with the platform in front of you. The horizontal angle allows heavy loading and full range of motion. It is excellent for building quad and glute size with reduced lower back stress.

en: Sit on a horizontal leg press machine with your back against the pad.
Place both feet on the platform shoulder-width apart.
Position your feet in the middle of the platform.
Release the safety stops.
Brace your core and grip the handles.
Press the platform forward by extending both legs.
Stop just short of locking out the knees.
Slowly lower the platform back to the start.
Allows heavy leg loading
Reduces lower back stress
Builds quad and glute size
Safe and stable setup
Strong leg hypertrophy move
Easy to learn and load

description.en: The side crunch with hands on chest is a side lying ab exercise that crunches the obliques without pulling on the neck. The hands on chest position keeps the move strict and isolates the side abs.

en: Lie on your side with legs stacked and slightly bent.
Cross both hands over your chest.
Place the bottom arm under the torso for support if needed.
Brace the obliques and lift the top shoulder off the floor.
Crunch the side body to lift the rib cage toward the hip.
Squeeze the obliques hard at the top.
Lower the shoulder back to the start with control.
Complete all reps on one side then switch sides.
Isolates the obliques without using the arms or neck.
Beginner friendly side core exercise.
Builds lateral core strength.
Improves rotational core control.
No equipment needed.
Easy to scale by changing leg position.

description.en: The side push up with towel is a sliding archer push up using a towel under one hand. The lifter performs a push up and slides one hand out wide on a towel as the body lowers. The slide creates a brutal one side dominant push up that loads the chest harder.

en: Place a small towel under one hand on a smooth floor.
Begin in a high plank position with hands under shoulders.
Brace your core and keep the body in a straight line.
Lower the body by bending the non towel arm.
At the same time slide the towel hand out wide to the side.
Continue until the chest reaches the bent elbow side.
Press back up using the bent arm and slide the towel hand back.
Switch sides between sets.
Brutal unilateral chest builder
No equipment beyond a towel
Trains shoulder stability
Builds the chest
Useful chest builder
Strong push up variation

description.en: The side-to-side jump rope is a jump-rope variation where you hop laterally (side to side) with each rope rotation rather than jumping straight up. The lateral movement adds hip and ankle conditioning and builds the lateral quickness that straight jumping misses.

en: Hold the jump rope handles. Start with feet together.
As the rope swings overhead, hop a few inches to the right, landing on both feet.
On the next rotation, hop a few inches to the left.
Continue alternating side to side with each rope swing.
Stay on the balls of your feet. Keep hops small and controlled.
Maintain a consistent rhythm. The lateral shift should be smooth.
Perform for time (1 to 3 minutes) or rounds.
Keep your core engaged and torso upright.
Adds lateral conditioning to jump rope training
Builds hip and ankle stability in the frontal plane
Develops coordination and rhythm
Excellent cardiovascular conditioning
More engaging than standard jumping
Needs only a jump rope

description.en: The sled 45-degree leg press is a compound lower-body machine exercise where you push a weighted sled up a 45-degree track using your legs. The guided path removes balance demand and allows extremely heavy loading of the quads and glutes with reduced lower-back involvement. It is one of the most popular leg-building machines in any gym.

en: Sit on the leg press machine with your back firmly against the pad. Place your feet on the platform shoulder-width apart, roughly in the center.
Release the safety handles and straighten your legs to take the weight. Do not lock your knees fully at the top.
Brace your core and keep your lower back pressed firmly against the pad throughout.
Lower the sled by bending at the knees and hips. Allow your knees to travel toward your chest.
Descend until your thighs reach roughly 90 degrees or until your lower back begins to round off the pad — stop before rounding.
Drive the sled back up by pressing through your full foot. Do not lock your knees at the top.
Adjust foot position: higher on the platform biases glutes/hamstrings, lower biases quads, wider biases adductors.
Re-engage the safety handles before exiting the machine.
Allows extremely heavy quad and glute loading in a guided path
Removes balance demand and upper-body involvement
Reduced lower-back stress compared to squats
Foot position adjustments bias different muscles
Allows safe training to failure with the safety stops
Easy to load progressively with plates

description.en: The Smith wide grip bench press combines a wide grip with the fixed bar path of a Smith machine. The wide hand position emphasizes the outer chest while the fixed path removes balance and stabilizing demands. It is a strong choice for chest specialization with heavier loads or higher reps.

en: Set up a flat bench under the Smith machine bar.
Lie back with eyes directly under the bar.
Grip the bar wider than your normal bench press grip.
Plant your feet flat and pull your shoulder blades back into the bench.
Unrack the bar by rotating your wrists.
Lower the bar with control to your upper chest.
Press the bar back up to lockout, squeezing your chest.
Re-rack the bar by rotating your wrists when finished.
Targets outer chest fibers
Fixed bar path removes balance demands
Allows focus on chest contraction
Useful for high-rep chest training
Beginner-friendly press variation
Heavier loading possible than free bar for many lifters

description.en: The standing behind-neck press is an overhead pressing variation where the barbell travels behind the head rather than in front. It shifts more emphasis to the lateral deltoid and reduces anterior deltoid involvement. However, it demands excellent shoulder mobility — lifters with limited mobility or shoulder issues should avoid this exercise.

en: Set a barbell at upper-chest height in a power rack. Step under the bar and place it across your upper traps behind your neck.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width. Step back from the rack.
Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart. Brace your core.
Press the bar straight up by extending at the elbows. Move your head slightly forward as the bar passes.
Lock out at the top with the bar directly above your shoulders.
Lower the bar slowly behind your head — only as low as your mobility allows. Stop at ear level or slightly lower.
Press back up to lockout. Repeat for the desired reps.
Use lighter weight than front pressing. Stop immediately if you feel shoulder discomfort.
Shifts emphasis to the lateral deltoid
Reduces anterior deltoid involvement
Builds shoulder width
Useful variation for advanced lifters
Trains shoulder mobility under load
Different stimulus than front pressing

description.en: The supine spinal twist (Supta Matsyendrasana) is a gentle restorative yoga pose where you lie on your back and let one knee fall across your body to the opposite side, creating a deep spinal rotation. It releases lower-back tension, stretches the glutes, and is one of the most calming twists in yoga.

en: Lie flat on your back with both legs extended and arms out to your sides at shoulder height (T-shape).
Bend your right knee and bring it across your body to the left side, lowering it toward the floor.
Keep your right shoulder pressed into the floor — do not let it lift.
Place your left hand on your right knee and gently press it toward the floor.
Turn your head to look toward your right hand.
Feel the gentle stretch through your right side, lower back, and glute.
Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply.
Return to center and repeat on the other side.
Gently rotates and decompresses the spine
Stretches the glutes and lower back
Releases tension from the entire torso
Calming and restorative
Excellent end-of-practice or pre-bed stretch
No equipment needed

description.en: The suspender crunch, also known as the TRX crunch, is performed with feet in the foot cradles of suspension straps and hands on the floor. From a plank position, you crunch the knees toward the chest. The instability of the straps adds significant core demand on top of the standard ab crunch.

en: Anchor suspension straps overhead with the foot cradles hanging at calf height.
Place your feet in the foot cradles and assume a high plank position.
Set your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor.
Brace your core hard.
Crunch your knees in toward your chest by rolling forward through the hips.
The straps will swing forward as you crunch.
Squeeze your abs hard at the top of the crunch.
Slowly extend your legs back to the plank position with control.
Builds core strength under instability
Strong ab and hip flexor engagement
Develops shoulder stability
Useful for athletes who need core control
Excellent for home or travel training
Easy to scale by changing strap length

description.en: The suspender twisting jack knife is a TRX core move that adds rotation to the standard knee tuck. The lifter pulls the knees in toward one shoulder, then alternates sides. It builds the obliques and rotational core strength.

en: Set the suspension trainer at hip height.
Place the feet in the straps with the soles up.
Set up in a high plank with hands under the shoulders.
Brace your core and keep the back flat.
Pull the knees forward and toward one shoulder.
Twist the hips at the top.
Extend the legs back to the start.
Repeat to the other side.
Loads the obliques
Trains rotation
Strong jack knife variation
Builds the core
Useful core builder

description.en: The table top bridge rotation combines a reverse table top hold with a thoracic rotation. The lifter holds the body up like a table while reaching one arm under and over. It builds the glutes, shoulders, and thoracic mobility.

en: Sit on the floor with the legs bent and feet flat.
Place the hands behind on the floor with fingers pointing back.
Lift the hips up so the torso is parallel with the floor.
Brace your core and squeeze the glutes.
Lift one hand off the floor.
Rotate the body to bring the hand under and across to the opposite side.
Reverse the rotation overhead and back to start.
Finish all reps then switch sides.
Builds the glutes
Trains rotation
Strong combo move
Useful for athletes
Builds shoulder mobility

description.en: The toe jump is a low-amplitude bouncing exercise where you stay on the balls of your feet and rapidly bounce in place. It builds calf endurance, ankle stiffness, and reactive strength — the same qualities trained by jump rope. It is excellent for warming up the lower legs before plyometric training.

en: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Stay on the balls of your feet — heels slightly off the floor.
Begin small, rapid bounces by extending and flexing your ankles only.
Keep your knees soft but mostly straight — the bounce comes from the ankles, not the knees.
Keep contact time with the floor as brief as possible — like a stiff spring.
Maintain rhythm and stay light on your feet.
Perform for 30 to 60 seconds per set.
Excellent warm-up before jump rope, sprints, or plyometrics.
Builds the calf endurance and ankle stiffness needed for jumping sports.
Builds calf endurance and ankle stiffness
Trains reactive strength in the lower legs
Excellent warm-up for plyometrics or running
No equipment needed
Improves cardiovascular conditioning
Foundation for advanced jumping skills

description.en: Walking on an incline treadmill is a high-intensity, low-impact cardio variation where you walk uphill at a steep grade (typically 5 to 15 percent). The incline dramatically increases calorie burn, builds the glutes, and elevates the heart rate without the joint impact of running. The popular "12-3-30" workout (12 percent incline, 3 mph, 30 minutes) is built on this principle.

en: Step onto the treadmill and straddle the belt. Set the incline to 5 to 12 percent.
Start the belt at a slow walking speed (1.5 to 2 mph) to begin.
Step onto the belt and begin walking. Stand tall — do not lean forward into the incline.
Gradually increase speed to a challenging but sustainable pace (typically 2.5 to 3.5 mph at high incline).
Avoid holding the handrails — this reduces calorie burn significantly. Use them only for balance if needed.
Pump your arms naturally for balance and added work.
Walk for the desired duration — typically 20 to 45 minutes.
Cool down with 2 to 3 minutes at a lower incline and slower pace.
Dramatically increases calorie burn vs flat walking
Builds the glutes and hamstrings effectively
Low-impact alternative to running
Excellent for fat loss
Builds cardiovascular endurance
Allows steady-state effort with minimal joint stress

description.en: Yoga Vajrasana, also known as thunderbolt or diamond pose, is a kneeling seated yoga posture. Sitting on the heels with a tall spine stretches the quads, ankles, and tops of the feet.

en: Kneel on the floor with the knees together.
Bring the big toes to touch behind you.
Lower the hips down to rest on the heels.
Sit tall and place the hands on the thighs.
Lengthen the spine through the crown of the head.
Relax the shoulders down and back.
Breathe slowly and steadily.
Hold the pose for the desired duration.
Stretches the quads and ankles.
Calms the mind in classical yoga practice.
Aids digestion when held after a meal.
No equipment needed.
Improves posture.
Excellent meditation pose.
